questiontext.text:
UniCV prototype for questions in which the student builds a flowchart with the shapes and the rules of Flowgorithm: variables declared with a type, arrays, functions with parameters and a return value, and the same operators and built-in functions. The grader runs the flowchart with the input of each test case and compares what it writes with the expected output, as in a programming question. For simpler flowcharts, without declarations or functions, use unicv_flowchart.

How to write a question

  1. Create a CodeRunner question of type unicv_flowgorithm, write the name and the question text, and save.
  2. In each test case, put the input data in Standard Input (one value per line) and the expected output in Expected output. Leave Test code empty.
  3. Build the solution flowchart in the Answer field and save with Validate on save ticked.
  4. For tall flowcharts, increase the number of rows of the answer box (Answer box, Rows).

What the student gets

  • An editor with the shapes of Flowgorithm (same colours and forms):
    • Input: reads one line of the test input into a variable (or an element of an array). The value must match the type of the variable.
    • Output: writes the value of an expression; by default it ends the line (this can be turned off).
    • Declare: creates variables of type Integer, Real, String or Boolean, or arrays with a size.
    • Assign: variable = expression.
    • Call: runs a function defined by the student.
    • Comment: a note in the flowchart; it has no effect on grading.
    • If, While, For (up or down, with a step) and Do (repeats while the condition is true, tested after).
  • At the top, the list of functions (Main and the student's own), the buttons "New function", "Properties" and delete function; on the right, the language of the editor (Portuguese, English or Spanish), "Start again" and "Help".
  • After Check, the usual CodeRunner table of tests, and the reason when the flowchart cannot run (e.g. a variable used before it is declared, or a value of the wrong type).

Rules (as in Flowgorithm)

  • Variables must be declared before they are used; / always gives a real, and a real stored in an Integer loses its decimal part; + only adds numbers and & joins texts; arrays start at position 0; names start with a letter, have only letters and digits, and are not case sensitive.
  • Operators: + - * / % mod ^, = == != <> < <= > >=, and && or || not !, &; constants true, false, pi.
  • Built-in functions: Abs, Sgn, Int, Sqrt, Ln, Log, Log10, Sin, Cos, Tan, Arcsin, Arccos, Arctan, Random, Len, Char, ToChar, ToCode, ToInteger, ToReal, ToString, ToFixed and Size.
  • Logical values are written true and false; reals with no decimal part are written without decimals.

Grading

  • Each test is passed when the output of the flowchart is exactly the expected output. With All-or-nothing grading (the default), the mark is 1 only if every test is passed.
  • The requirements in exigir, proibir and funcoes (see below) are checked before running the tests.

Limitations

  • The Flowgorithm shapes used only for debugging (Breakpoint), turtle graphics and files are not included.
  • Random gives different values on each run, so tests should not depend on its result.
  • The flowchart is stored as JSON in the answer; it cannot be imported from or exported to Flowgorithm (.fprg) files.

Template parameters (all optional)

  • exigir / proibir: lists of shapes that the flowchart must use / must not use, among "entrada", "saida", "declarar", "atribuicao", "chamar", "se", "enquanto", "para", "fazer", "comentario" and "ciclo" (any loop). The English names are also accepted.
  • funcoes: list of the names of the functions the student must define, e.g. ["Quadrado"].
  • max_passos (default 100000): largest number of shapes run in each test, to detect endless loops.
  • lang (default "pt"): language of the error messages when the student has not chosen another one in the editor: "pt", "en" or "es".

Example: {"exigir": ["para"], "funcoes": ["Fatorial"]}
